provenance.note: Measured at load 2.68 after the NCC hot-loop change (b1d74bf): four accumulator chains in prepare_chip! and integral_both!, ifelse for the denominator guard, FFTW_PATIENT plans. The change helps serially and not under threading, which a direct A/B of the eager row against its parent b4fb528 settles -- same machine, back to back, identical 920544 points: 1 thread 74.29 s -> 66.26 s (1.12x), 12 threads 24.67 s -> 25.40 s (1.03x SLOWER). So the 33-35 s 12-thread row here is not a regression from the change, and equally the change buys nothing there: at 12 threads this workload is bound by memory bandwidth rather than by the arithmetic the change removed, so cheaper points do not shorten it. Quote the serial row for the optimization and the threaded row for throughput; they answer different questions. An earlier revision of this note blamed the 12-thread number on machine contention. That was wrong and is retracted: two runs at load 3.45 and 2.68 agree to 4%, and the A/B above reproduces the threaded result at both commits. What remains unexplained is that this row achieves ~2.85 cores where the 8d7c1ec run recorded 3.78; base and HEAD both sit at ~2.85 today, so whatever moved it is not this change. The 4096 lazy row peaked at 9784 MiB against 3654 at 2048: 25 blocks on 12 threads holds twelve 6144-pixel working sets at once, which measures the block size being large relative to the scene rather than what blocking costs. 8192 is excluded for the same reason at 9 blocks.
